1.title: Rebase and Tidy History
1.text: Welcome to Module five: Rebase and Tidy History. It covers the exam area Part two: Branching and history. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do seven things. Rebase a branch onto a new base. Continue, skip or abort a ree base that hits a conflict. Clean up commits with amend, interactive ree base, fixup and autosquash. Move a branch with --onto. Use pull --rebase. Know when not to ree base. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: What a rebase does
1.text: What a ree base does. A ree base replays your commits on a new base. On your feature branch you run git ree base main. Git sets your commits aside, moves the branch to the tip of main, and applies the commits again, one by one.

1.text: What a ree base does. The figure shows this: A feature branch with two commits is replayed on top of the new tip of main, so the history becomes one straight line and the replayed commits get new hashes.

1.title: What a rebase does, continued
1.text: What a ree base does. Each replayed commit has a new parent, so it is a new commit with a new hash. The change it makes is the same. Changes (the patch). The same. Message, author, author date. The same. Parent. New: the tip of main. Hash. New, for every replayed commit. main. Not moved. Old commits. Still in the repository (reflog). The history is now one straight line. Merging the branch into main afterward is a fast-forward. Tip: Stand on your own branch and ree base it onto the target. git ree base main moves the branch you are on and never changes main.

1.title: Conflicts during a rebase
1.text: Conflicts during a ree base. A ree base applies commits one at a time, so it can stop at any commit with a conflict. Git names the commit it could not apply. You fix the file, then choose how to go on. git add file then git ree base the continue flag. Keep your resolved version and replay the next commit. git ree base the skip flag. Drop the commit that conflicts and go on. git ree base the abort flag. Stop and put the branch back exactly as it was before. Try it. Resolve one conflict and continue.

1.title: Conflicts during a rebase, continued
1.text: Conflicts during a ree base. Between git status and git add, you edit prices dot txt and remove the markers. Status says "interactive ree base in progress" even for a plain ree base. During a ree base the upper half of the markers ( head ) is the branch you ree base onto, and the lower half is your commit being replayed. That is the reverse of what many people expect. The same swap applies to git checkout the ours flag and the theirs flag: during a ree base, the ours flag is the branch you ree base onto and the theirs flag is your own commit (in a merge it is the other way round, module four).

1.title: Conflicts during a rebase, continued
1.text: Conflicts during a ree base. If several commits change the same lines, the ree base stops once for each. In the lab, three such commits stopped it three times, and after squashing them it stopped once. Tip: When a ree base gets confusing, run git ree base the abort flag. It restores the branch exactly.

1.title: Tidy history before you share it
1.text: Tidy history before you share it. Amend. git commit the amend flag replaces the last commit: stage a forgotten file first, then amend. the no edit flag keeps the message and dash m sets a new one. The result is a new hash. Interactive ree base. git ree base dash i main opens a todo list with one line per commit, oldest first (the reverse of git log ). You change the first word of a line or move lines, then save and close.

1.title: Tidy history before you share it, continued
1.text: Tidy history before you share it. pick. Keep the commit as it is. reword. Keep the changes, edit the message. squash. Meld into the commit above and keep both messages for you to edit. fixup. Meld into the commit above and discard this message. drop. Delete the commit and its changes. Move a line. Reorder the commits. A change to one commit gives every later commit a new hash. The lab edits the list with a script set in git sequence editor. Try it. Squash a typo fix and drop a debug commit. Your edited list is shown first.

1.title: Tidy history before you share it, continued
1.text: Tidy history before you share it. Fixup and autosquash. Record a fix as a commit that names its target: git commit the fixup flag hash creates a commit titled fixup! subject. Then git ree base dash i the autosquash flag main moves it under the target and marks it fixup for you. The setting ree base dot auto Squash true makes this the default for dash i. Try it. git sequence editor true accepts the prepared list without opening an editor.

1.title: Move a branch, pull with rebase, and the golden rule
1.text: Move a branch, pull with ree base, and the golden rule. the onto flag replays only part of a branch somewhere else: git ree base the onto flag new base old base branch. Example: topic was started from feature, and feature was then squash-merged into main. A plain git ree base main on topic replays the old feature commits too, and in the lab it stopped on a conflict. git ree base the onto flag main feature topic replays only the commits after feature, which are the commits of topic. The branch feature is left untouched.

1.title: Move a branch, pull with rebase, and the golden rule, continued
1.text: Move a branch, pull with ree base, and the golden rule. git pull the ree base flag fetches the new commits from the remote and replays your unpushed commits on top of them. The history stays linear, with no merge commit. Module seven covers pull in full. The golden rule: never ree base commits that others already have. A ree base replaces commits, and a teammate's copy of an old commit does not match its new copy. In the lab, Ada ree based a branch she had pushed. A plain git push was rejected as a non-fast-forward. git push the force with lease flag published the rewritten branch.

2.title: Move a branch, pull with rebase, and the golden rule, continued
2.text: Move a branch, pull with ree base, and the golden rule. Bob's fetch reported a forced update. His merge pull kept both versions, so the commit appeared twice. Cy, with no work of his own, ran git reset the hard flag origin slash feature slash search and matched the remote. History shape. Merge: Keeps real branching and adds a merge commit. Rebase: One straight line, no merge commit. Existing commits. Merge: Untouched. Rebase: Replaced by new commits with new hashes. Conflicts. Merge: Resolved once. Rebase: May stop at every replayed commit. Safe on a shared branch. Merge: Yes. Rebase: No.

2.title: Move a branch, pull with rebase, and the golden rule, continued
2.text: Move a branch, pull with ree base, and the golden rule. Undo. Merge: Revert the merge (module six). Rebase: orig head or the reflog. Best for. Merge: Joining finished work into a shared branch. Rebase: Tidying a private branch, catching up with main. Tip: Rebase your private branch freely; once others have it, merge instead. If you must rewrite a pushed branch, use the force with lease flag and tell your team.

2.title: Recovering from a bad rebase
2.text: Recovering from a bad ree base. A ree base does not delete the old commits at once. Two ways back. orig head holds the branch tip from before the ree base. Run git reset the hard flag orig head right after the ree base. A later reset or ree base overwrites it. The reflog keeps a history of where each branch pointed. feature slash search at one is the position before the last change. Try it. Undo the ree base from section one.

2.title: Practice Question 1
2.text: Question one. After git ree base main, the log shows the same two messages as before, but all the hashes changed. What explains this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Each commit was replayed on a new parent, so it is a new commit. A commit's hash includes its parent, so replaying on a new base creates new commits with the same changes.

2.title: Practice Question 2
2.text: Question two. A ree base stops with "could not apply d nine f eight three six six... Discount the price". You have fixed prices dot txt and removed the markers. What do you run next? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: git add prices dot txt, then git ree base the continue flag. You stage the resolved file and continue, while the skip flag would drop that commit and your fix with it.

2.title: Practice Question 3
2.text: Question three. Ada ree based feature slash search, which she and Bob had both pushed and pulled. Her git push is rejected as a non-fast-forward. What is the safest next step? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Run git push the force with lease flag, then tell Bob to reset. The lease refuses if someone else pushed in the meantime, and Bob must reset because his copy holds the old commits.

2.title: Practice Question 4
2.text: Question four. A branch has the commits "Add cart", "Fix typo" and "W I P". You want the last two folded into "Add cart", with their messages discarded. Which word goes before them in the todo list? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: fixup, which melds it in and discards its message. fixup melds a commit into the one above and throws its message away, while squash keeps the message.

2.title: Practice Question 5
2.text: Question five. git reflog show feature lists feature at zero ree base finish above feature at one commit Add results page. The ree base was a mistake. How do you get the old branch back? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Reset the branch hard to feature at one. The entry before ree base finish is the old tip, and a hard reset moves the branch back to it.

2.title: Practice Question 6
2.text: Question six. topic was started from feature, and feature was squash-merged into main. A plain git ree base main on topic conflicts. Which command replays only the commits of topic? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: git ree base the onto flag main feature topic. the onto flag new base old base branch replays the commits after feature on top of main.

2.title: Recall Check 1
2.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What does git ree base main do to the commits of your branch? Answer: It replays them on top of main as new commits with new hashes. Question two. Which three options control a ree base that stopped on a conflict? Answer: the continue flag, the skip flag and the abort flag. Question three. Which command creates a commit that autosquash folds into an earlier one? Answer: git commit the fixup flag hash.

2.title: Recall Check 2
2.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Which command replaces the last commit instead of adding a new one? Answer: git commit the amend flag. Question five. What does git pull the ree base flag do with your unpushed commits? Answer: It replays them on top of the fetched commits, with no merge commit. Question six. What is the golden rule of ree basing? Answer: Never ree base commits that others already have.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. Rebase: git ree base main replays your commits on the tip of main; new hashes; straight history. Conflict: stops per commit; fix, git add, the continue flag; or the skip flag; or the abort flag. Markers: during a ree base the upper half ( head ) is the branch you ree base onto. Todo list: pick, reword, squash, fixup, drop; oldest commit first; move lines to reorder. Amend: git commit the amend flag replaces the last commit; the no edit flag keeps the message. Autosquash: git commit the fixup flag hash, then git ree base dash i the autosquash flag main. Onto: git ree base the onto flag new base old base branch replays only the commits after the old base. Pull: git pull the ree base flag replays your local commits on the fetched ones.
